gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: I'd rather ___ by card than carry cash.
gaps.explanation: pay by card/in cash is the fixed pattern for the method of payment.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: The jury was unable to ___ a decision.
gaps.explanation: reach a decision is the fixed collocation; 'arrive' needs 'at' and cannot be followed directly by the object.

gaps.sentence: The children ___ great fun at the fair.
The two sides struggled to ___ an agreement before the deadline.
Our guide was highly ___ and had climbed the mountain five times.
gaps.explanation: highly experienced is the standard collocation; 'highly' combines with participial adjectives.
